notes.title: Major Overhaul of Skill Reservation and Macro System
notes.content:
"Convenience as a baseline, where player's strategic decisions shine."


Hello, this is Mocha and Latte from the Chaos Bringer development team back again.

Following our previous dev note about the smarter 'Movement System,' today we're excited to reveal the final version of the much-anticipated 'Macro' feature and how it was completed.



Actually, we've discussed the initial concept of macros in a previous dev note. For those whose memory might be a bit hazy, let me give you a quick recap.
Previously on Macro Development:
Breaking the Click Curse: To eliminate the inconvenience of constantly clicking on targets, we designed a 'Target Caching' feature where the system remembers targets and players only need to press skill buttons twice.
Macros to Reduce Repetition: Going further, we proposed an initial version that bundles multiple skills into a single 'macro' skill that can be used repeatedly.
Remaining Limitations: However, even this approach had the limitation of being another form of repetitive action that required 'constantly pressing the macro button again.'
So after internal testing, we completely turned this concept on its head. 
Let me now introduce our new solution to eliminate 'repetitive actions' entirely.
1. Macros: One reservation, infinite repetition.

Let me cut to the chase, 
Now macros only need to be reserved once, and they'll repeat infinitely until the player issues another command.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/1096181953fa04b0a497c3a9da6b23d58d651907.gif"]
Once combat begins, just activate the macro once. After that, players can focus solely on reading the battlefield, avoiding danger, and making strategic decisions to manually use skills at critical moments. 


No more need to repeatedly press the macro button!


2. "Why was my character idle?" - Timeline UI Overhaul


With macros repeating infinitely, it became crucial to understand what skills characters are currently using and what they'll use next.

The existing timeline in the upper left corner had visibility issues, as players focused on the center of the screen where battles occur. Many of you experienced "I thought I reserved skills, but why is my character just standing there?" only to check the timeline belatedly.



To solve this problem, we moved the skill reservation timeline above each character's head.

Timeline expanding above selected character: The skill reservation list for your currently selected character expands clearly above their head. You can immediately see what skills will be executed next.

Minimized view for other characters: Timelines for unselected characters smoothly collapse and minimize, but you can still clearly see that multiple skills are queued up.

Intuitive macro skill distinction: Skill icons reserved by macros display "MACRO" text, making them easily distinguishable from manually reserved skills. (Of course, this text display is temporary design that may change with our designer's touch!)

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/d2f14269ce06e891512e2ee48572441a48443ad6.gif"]

No need to worry about not knowing exactly when skills will be cast with the timeline position change. Hovering your mouse over each skill icon shows a tooltip with the exact cast start time (MM:SS.s), allowing you to check whenever precise control is needed.


3. Moments of Strategic Decision: Priority between Macros and Manual Skills


Of course, convenient macros shouldn't interfere with players' strategic choices. 

Our skill reservation system has the following clear priorities:

Normal skill reservation: Always takes priority over macros. When players manually reserve skills, the automatically running macro cycle pauses and executes that skill first.

Priority skill reservation (Shift + Click): Commands for emergency situations that must be executed before any other action. Use this to interrupt enemy casting or apply survival skills to allies, and it will prepare to activate immediately, ignoring all reservations.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/ad8f771342199841ebe875d2f4d18261215bfb5d.gif"]
This allows you to enjoy the convenience of 'infinitely repeating macros with one reservation' normally, while your sharp judgment can immediately intervene in combat at critical moments.
As a small tip, right-clicking skill icons displayed above characters' heads will immediately cancel that skill reservation or active macro.
[hr][/hr]
Stay tuned for the next dev note!

So far we've explained how our macro system 'works.' That leaves the most important question, right?
"So how do players actually create these amazing macros?"
We're currently working hard on developing a 'Macro Creation' feature that allows you to save, edit, and even set icons for your own optimized skill cycles. 
We'll cover this exciting news in detail in the next dev note, so please look forward to it!
We'll continue listening to your feedback and creating better gaming experiences.

Thank you.

notes.title: Combat Tension Through Animation: The Target Focus System in Chaos Bringer
notes.content:
Hello! I'm Cherish, a designer at Sayberry Games.

First of all, I sincerely apologize for not sharing development news for such a long time. We promised monthly updates, but now we're back after two months. I apologize to everyone who has been waiting.

During this time, our team has been working tirelessly to improve the quality of the game. We've thoroughly refactored existing systems and invested a lot of time in creating more intuitive and user-friendly gameplay. There's still a lot we can't show yet, but significant progress has been made - please be patient a little longer.

We're paying attention to every small detail to meet your expectations. As part of these efforts, today, following our previous camera system improvements, I'll explain in detail how we designed our character animation system.

The "Focus" System for Enemies
Chaos Bringer has a "focus" system. All party members can be set to focus on one enemy, and whenever they use attack skills, they automatically target this "focus target."
This means you don't need to set a target for each character every time you use a skill. It's a system many of you are already familiar with from the world-famous game WoW (World of Warcraft)!

This feature can be represented through the UI, but what if we go further and intuitively show through character movements "who will attack which enemy"? In other words, creating an animation system where all focused characters continuously look at their targets while moving. This allows players to instantly see which enemies our heroes are focusing on, and character movements appear smarter and more tense.

Difference from Traditional Overhead Camera Games
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/82add7fd98a28af626a862de069af4a7b8e09d07.png
In typical overhead camera games, characters don't look at enemies while moving.
Since they look in the direction of movement, they often appear like robots or chess pieces.
More precisely, they appear to move without free will, only as controlled. Most games adopt this approach because there's no specific "focus target." Since characters don't have a specific target to look at, they're designed to simply face the "movement direction" when moving.

So what about our game, where a clear "focus target" exists and needs to be displayed intuitively?
In our game, characters need to stare at the "focus target" while also being "able to move freely". This means the "looking direction" and "movement direction" don't always match and must be completely separated in animation.
For example, characters should be able to move sideways while looking at an enemy, and when retreating, they can walk backwards while continuing to watch the enemy.

A Movement System that Enhances Combat Immersion
Actually, this movement concept isn't new. It's already widely used in many beloved and familiar games. Examples include third-person shooters (TPS) and Souls-like games.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/fe629cc88c10c300f9804711ce7b611843094580.png
In these games, characters aren't restricted to moving only in the direction the player is looking. They can always observe the screen direction controlled by the player's mouse while freely moving forward/backward/left/right with the keyboard.

We adopted this locomotion system and applied it in our own way. We provide the same freedom of movement but chose a method where characters "stare at the focus target while moving" instead of following the mouse pointer.
Thanks to this, characters don't just move according to commands but give the feeling of moving while being aware of enemies.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/8beba709492e8d30f43723359993d574fe83ed5c.gif

We believe this movement method not only increases immersion but also helps express battle situations more intuitively - especially important for the real-time with pause (RTwP) nature where time often needs to be stopped. When a character casts a skill, you can intuitively see who it will be cast on.
When all characters look at and move toward one enemy, players naturally recognize that target as the most important. This phenomenon of jointly looking at what someone else is watching is called "Joint Attention."

Technical Approach for Natural Movement
To implement these movements naturally, we use Unreal Engine's Blend Space system. Blend Space is a feature that blends multiple animation movements.

First, we collect appropriate strafe animations for characters in various directions. Then we calculate the movement direction from player input and blend the collected strafe movements that match that direction to create new movement animations. We apply this created movement only to the character's lower body. Finally, we make the upper body always face the target to be observed, and we get the desired final result.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/4b5881ec59a7b943760e282b25440c020a2adec5.gif

Future Plans...
Additionally, we plan to implement "turn animations where characters realistically turn when the focus target changes". Actually, we already tested this in our previous engine before switching game engines. This will naturally connect character movements even when the focus target changes.

That was our introduction to the animation system. What do you think?
With this more lively and informative animation system, we designed characters to appear not as simple objects but as organic beings that read and react to the flow of combat.

Working on such fine details may seem trivial, but it actually requires significant time and effort. However, we're confident these efforts will provide you with a truly immersive gaming experience.

Once again, I apologize for not sharing news for so long. We'll try to share development updates more frequently in the future. To meet your expectations, we're focusing on quality rather than rushing, concentrating on creating an enjoyable and satisfying experience from the player's perspective.

Thank you for your continued interest and support. We'll be back soon with more development news. We look forward to your anticipation!

notes.title: Camera System Development Story
notes.content:
Hello! This is Cherish, a designer at Savory Games. I’m in charge of designing art and user interaction, as well as implementing and testing them in Unreal. You can think of me as someone who wears multiple hats: art, UI design, and a technical artist role.

Chaosbringer is based on the somewhat unfamiliar RTwP system—Real-Time with Pause. Because of this, there seem to be many fresh considerations and attempts when it comes to controls and usability. I have a lot of concerns as well, and I’d like to introduce the direction that has been shaped through discussions with various users and our own team members.

Overview
I believe that “usability” is the most important aspect of an RTwP game. Once the action pauses in the midst of intense combat, players need to be able to intervene in a more detailed and appropriate manner. Also, because this system is unfamiliar to many, it can create a high entry barrier. That’s why we listened to a variety of opinions at GLS2024 and, based on that, have revamped many systems. In this post, I’d like to talk about the camera system as part of those improvements.

The camera, which can be called the “player’s eyes,” is a crucial element. Vision is responsible for the first stage—“perception.” Just as we can easily perceive the world around us without much effort, camera control should also be unconscious and intuitive, almost like breathing. At the same time, it would be great to have certain helpful features so players can easily respond to the various situations that arise in an RTwP game.

Direction of Improvement

Reduce Degrees of Freedom (DOF)!
“Reducing degrees of freedom” might sound negative, but simplifying controls by reducing freedom of movement is actually a common concept. Doesn’t it feel a bit unsafe to have just a set of stairs in a wide-open space? Installing handrails at both ends and indicating the path on the floor would make it much more comfortable. Similarly, in our already complex game, giving too many control options can increase mental load, which is not desirable. To make the fundamental act of “looking” intuitive, camera control must be simple yet effective.

Especially in a 3D space, there are many freedoms we can remove. For example, going below the ground or zooming too high into the sky doesn’t provide meaningful value—it’s merely “inconvenient freedom.” Preventing such movements while smoothly guiding players in the direction our game demands is the key point of this improvement.

Avoid Anything Too New, Evoke Familiar Controls
We aim for a camera system that feels new, yet somehow familiar to users. This way, they can immediately dive into the fun of the game without additional learning. In other words, while our camera system’s underlying approach is innovative, the controls and feedback that players “feel” should be familiar. That’s how control becomes as “natural as breathing.”

To achieve this, we didn’t create an entirely new control method. Instead, we adopted a strategy of carefully combining and improving existing, effective camera control methods. However, the crux is to ensure that players can subconsciously switch to the most suitable method quickly and easily depending on the situation.

How Did We Improve It?

Three Core Views in Chaosbringer’s Gameplay

1. Overhead View
Observe the situation from a high vantage point and select a desired character or object.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/ce5c2ea79c9376cb2b2e46ccb3466fefd54b708a.png

2. Battlefield View
View the field from the characters’ or party’s perspective, immersing yourself more deeply in the combat situation.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/8d2d44d99eae3fc6009eb8141d2d6f0c5bbebeac.png

3. Observation View
Zoom in on a particular character or monster for a detailed look.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/33b3873fbe198c6a8830fcf5f6d994386c53a756.png

Smart Zoom: A Camera Moving Along a Spline Rail
Our zoom in/out is not just about physically getting the camera closer.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/67552ed83af88bccf8fb05b637b9f7f2cb398378.png

When zooming in, the camera follows a specific curve, appearing to pull back slightly while keeping the focus fixed. Because it only moves along this specialized curve, it won’t go below the ground or too high into the sky—i.e., it won’t wander into pointless spaces—and instead quickly provides multiple useful views. Meanwhile, players can simply use the mouse wheel to zoom in/out and move freely among these varied viewpoints.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/b1e1217923c580ffa9e3f32eeb2f575439e93532.gif
For example, when moving from “1. Overhead View” to “2. Battlefield View,” it’s not just a simple zoom-in. The camera shifts horizontally toward the character’s front view, allowing a closer approach. Through this, the player doesn’t just watch the heroes but actually feels as though they are looking at the enemies together with the heroes, providing an increased sense of immersion.

Panning and Rotation

The possibilities don’t end here.
Our camera system allows you to pan across the battlefield horizontally and also rotate (orbit) around the point you are looking at.

Panning is done freely via WASD.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/9ac40e092c30ce70e20281506359b8105797217e.gif

You can also move the camera with a left mouse click if necessary.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/265999728a310a8740207c97d251893060b435e6.gif

Rotation is performed by holding down the right mouse button and dragging.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/c7837dc1dc52148e485096883e918ca474297f7f.gif

Additionally, if a certain option is enabled, dragging the right mouse button up/down will zoom in/out, while dragging left/right will perform rotation.

By combining these options, you can freely rotate the camera view with right-click dragging as if in an FPS game (albeit along our “optimized” path), allowing players familiar with FPS controls to play comfortably.

Natural Switching Between Free Mode and Lock-On Mode

Free Cam Mode: Right-click to rotate + WASD to pan + Mouse wheel to zoom
Our camera system basically allows rotation by holding the right mouse button. In that state, WASD panning and mouse wheel zoom in/out are still available. These controls do not conflict with each other, so the player can comfortably perform all three simultaneously.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/a2976dc3d023111aaa4a6c30b5cb8b49611ef9a1.gif

This provides an experience similar to a “spectator mode” familiar from other games. In this mode, you can freely survey the battlefield, observe specific characters/monsters, and enjoy a continuous camera experience. You can also record the ongoing combat in real time for stunning footage.

Even while moving around so freely, you can quickly return to the desired angle. Essentially, the camera moves along an optimized path. Furthermore, if you combine this with focusing on a specific character’s viewpoint, you can get back to the battlefield even faster!

Soft Lock-On Mode
We refer to camera focus on a specific character as Soft Lock-On. In this state, without panning, you can conveniently zoom in/out and rotate using the mouse.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/13d10a4de04c5231755040ca3c6112bdb66f4eae.gif

Additionally, we plan to expand this fixed view to include Hard Lock-On Mode, where the camera remains locked onto a specific character, following them continuously. We’ve tested this mode at GLS, and we expect it to offer an immersive experience, reminiscent of classic TRPGs, especially in single-player dungeons. We’ll share more detailed plans and development updates in a future post!

Going Forward…
That’s it for our camera revamp. What did you think?

We are continuously testing this system internally and plan to gather feedback whenever we have the chance to let external users play. We know well that to enhance our unique RTwP system, we must harmoniously improve not just the camera, but also UI, interaction, controls, and many other elements. We’ll be doing a lot of thinking and improvements in the future!

We hope you’ll look forward to our ongoing changes and growth even more than our current state. With that, I’ll sign off here.
Thank you!

notes.title: Revamped Combat System: Smoother and More Strategic Gameplay
notes.content:
Hi, nice to meet you! We are Moka and Latte, the development team behind Chaos Bringer.
After dedicating a lot of effort, we’re excited to share news about a major update to our combat system.

Movement and Skill Reservation System Overhaul
We’ve revamped the movement and skill reservation systems to eliminate the hassle and stress of controlling movement!

1. Allies Considered Obstacles Based on Context
Previously, allies were always considered non-obstacles, which meant that if an ally blocked another ally’s path, players had to manually reposition them.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/ddb7e519e4eacbd8fcee0ea023b8d0ea36d0b7d0.gif

To improve this, we’ve updated the system to determine allies as obstacles or non-obstacles based on the situation.


Allies considered obstacles when:

Casting a skill
Standing idle
Blocking a path for more than 0.1 seconds


Allies considered non-obstacles when:

Combat begins
Moving or movement is reserved
Just finished an action



2. Real-time Path Updates During Movement
In the old algorithm, optimal paths were calculated only when the movement command was first issued, meaning it didn’t adapt to changes. We’ve enhanced it to increase the points when paths are recalculated:

When the movement command is issued
After moving one tile
When a path is blocked for more than 0.1 seconds

This makes movement more fluid and responsive to changes.

3. Skill Reservation Now Possible for Out-of-Range Targets
Previously, you could only reserve skills for targets within skill range. This forced players to frequently pause combat to reposition, even in scenarios meant for skill "reservation." 
Now, you can reserve skills for out-of-range targets.


In-range targets: Skills are executed immediately.
Out-of-range targets:

Automatically calculates the optimal path and destination for the skill.
Updates the path if the target moves during transit.
Executes the skill as soon as it comes within range.


No more pausing the game just to handle skill range issues!

Macro and Target Caching Features Added
Eliminate the stress of repetitive actions and focus solely on strategic decisions!

1. Old System: Assign Skills and Targets for Every Ally
Players had to manually select skills and targets for every ally repeatedly.
[olist]
Select an ally.
Click skill → target → skill → target... repeat endlessly.
Repeat the same process for every ally.
[/olist]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/fafe2f521c96c6675b10bb90bb277bc335cd9f62.gif

2. Target Caching: No More Manual Target Selection

Auto-assign logical targets: Targets are cached per hero based on previous choices or logical defaults like the nearest or attacking enemy.
Execute skills with shortcut keys: Pressing the skill shortcut key again will confirm the cached target and use the skill.
[olist]
Select an ally.
Skill * 2 → Skill * 2 → Skill * 2... repeat.
Repeat the process for other allies.
[/olist]

No need to manually select targets every time!

3. Macro Feature: Save Custom Skill Cycles
Players naturally develop their own skill cycles as heroes grow. Why not save those cycles for easy reuse in repetitive battles?

The macro feature is designed to help players store and reuse their optimal skill cycles for each character.

Routine skill rotations: Save basic combat actions like attacks or buffs without repeated setup.
Logical target assignment: Cache logical targets per hero for seamless execution.
Emergency control flexibility: Focus only on critical actions like blocking, dodging, or using potions when necessary.


Combat Preparation: Save Skill Cycles Per Class
Macros are saved by class and can be shared across heroes of the same class. Players can create multiple macros to prepare for various battle scenarios.
[olist]
Macro creation: Store custom skill cycles as macros in your skill book. Save over 10 skills in a sequence!
Shortcut assignment: Assign macros to hotkeys for easy execution.
[/olist]

Combat Start: Execute Skills with Macros
With macros, the basic combat process becomes simpler:
[olist]
Select an ally.
Execute macros (e.g., Macro * 2 → Macro * 2 → Macro * 2... repeat).
Repeat for other allies.
[/olist]
A single macro execution reserves multiple skills and targets seamlessly.

4. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to Select Allies
Quickly cycle through allies using the Tab or Shift+Tab keys. No need to click party lists, maps, or awkwardly stretch for function keys.

Eliminate unnecessary pauses and control stress! Check out the upgraded combat in the gameplay video below.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/d89f5c94383d7bcf5ad3e345d37ff3241ae750a5.gif

notes.title: Innovative Combat System: The Perfect Balance Between Turn-Based and Real-Time
notes.content:
Hello! I’m Chaos, the system and balance designer for ChaosBringer. Today, I’m thrilled to share an in-depth look at one of our game’s core features: the Real-Time with Pause (RTwP) combat system. From RTwP’s history and recent developments to diverse player perspectives, I’ll explain why we chose this system and how we’re innovating it.

The Journey of RTwP: From Glory Days to Challenging Times

The origins of RTwP date back to 1998 with none other than Baldur's Gate. BioWare wanted to capture the complexity of D&D rules in a computer RPG while retaining the dynamism of real-time strategy. The result was RTwP, which revolutionized the RPG genre! Since then, classics like Planescape: Torment, the Icewind Dale series, and the legendary Baldur's Gate 2 have adopted this system.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/bb3380dbe2840606c895ccaf6d2164b68d255ec1.jpg The original Baldur's Gate, which popularized RTwP in CRPGs

In the early 2000s, RTwP and turn-based combat were the two main pillars of CRPGs. Games like Knights of the Old Republic, Neverwinter Nights, and Dragon Age: Origins offered both deep strategy and the thrill of real-time combat, gaining widespread acclaim.

But nothing’s perfect. Some players found late-game combat tedious, reduced to “auto-attacking.” Others struggled to effectively manage every character in complex combat scenarios.

Changes in the CRPG Market and the Challenge for RTwP

By the mid-2010s, the success of Divinity: Original Sin brought renewed attention to turn-based combat. Attracted by turn-based systems’ clarity and simplicity, developers began to shift toward this approach in RPGs.

However, RTwP wasn’t completely forgotten. The Pillars of Eternity series from Obsidian Entertainment continued the RTwP legacy, adding modern touches that resonated with fans. But with the addition of a turn-based mode in Pillars of Eternity 2, change was on the horizon.

The Bold Shift in Baldur’s Gate 3 {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/d41280a654b883162ad9de7124908597ce9cc999.jpg Baldur’s Gate series fully transformed into turn-based combat

In 2023, the launch of Baldur’s Gate 3 shocked fans by adopting a fully turn-based system, despite RTwP being synonymous with the series. While many wondered, “Is this really Baldur’s Gate?” the game’s massive success showed a shift in the market.

Gradual Change in the Pathfinder Series {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/36abd1f9f098f5d432a19a5b3c54e8380564818a.jpg The turn-based mode introduced in Pillars of Eternity 2

The Pathfinder series by Owlcat Games illustrates this transition well. Kingmaker (2018) employed RTwP, while Wrath of the Righteous (2021) adopted a hybrid system. And the upcoming The Dragon’s Demand has announced it will exclusively use turn-based combat. Josh Sawyer, director of the Pillars of Eternity series, recently commented on RTwP’s limitations, mentioning he would consider turn-based if there were to be a Pillars 3, a statement that stirred RTwP supporters.

Such changes have left RTwP fans feeling a sense of loss, with some lamenting the decline of the classic CRPG essence.

But does this mean the end of RTwP, or is it preparing for a new evolution? The debate among players continues.

The Community’s Voice on RTwP

2020 Poll by Andy Kelly

In 2020, shortly before the release of Baldur’s Gate 3, PC Gamer’s Andy Kelly conducted a poll asking readers, “Which do you prefer: RTwP or turn-based?” The results were close, with 46.4% preferring RTwP and 53.6% preferring turn-based. Although turn-based was slightly more popular, RTwP still had strong support.

Player Feedback on RTwP

I also gathered various opinions from online forums and gaming communities, gaining valuable insights into RTwP’s pros and cons. This feedback has greatly helped us improve our system.

💡 Advantages of RTwP

Perfect blend of strategy and speed: RTwP offers the strategic depth of turn-based combat with the excitement of real-time action. Complex battles can be planned carefully, while simpler fights can be completed quickly.
Flexible difficulty adjustment: Players can control the pace of combat based on their skill level and preferences. Skilled players can dominate battles with minimal pausing, while cautious players can pause frequently to execute detailed strategies.
Enhanced immersion: Real-time combat feels more dynamic and realistic, especially in large-scale battles.
⚠️ Disadvantages of RTwP

Complexity and confusion: Managing multiple characters simultaneously can be overwhelming.
UI challenges: Some RTwP games suffer from complex UIs that disrupt the gameplay, making players spend more time navigating the UI than fighting.
Limited strategic depth: The real-time nature can make it difficult to control every detail, potentially reducing strategic depth.
Why RTwP Now?

The RPG market is now filled with turn-based systems. Since the success of the Divinity: Original Sin series, many games have chosen turn-based combat, even Baldur’s Gate 3. Watching a legendary RTwP series transition to turn-based disappointed many fans, myself included.

Honestly, we also considered our options. But RTwP has a unique appeal that we couldn’t ignore. We are now confident: RTwP is the best system to achieve the gameplay experience we’re aiming for. And in 2024, with turn-based RPGs dominating the market, we are proud to raise the RTwP flag high again in ChaosBringer.

RTwP’s Appeal

Unbroken combat flow RTwP provides strategic depth without interrupting the flow of combat. In turn-based games, each turn pauses the action, but in RTwP, battles continue seamlessly, creating a sense of urgency like a real battlefield.

Perfect balance of reflex and strategy RTwP tests both the player’s reflexes and strategic thinking. You need to assess situations quickly and make decisions, leading to a dynamic and challenging gameplay experience.

Supports diverse playstyles RTwP supports different playstyles. Experienced players can control battles with minimal pausing, while cautious players can pause frequently to control every detail.

ChaosBringer’s Innovative RTwP System

Our RTwP system is different from the past. We’ve worked hard to maximize RTwP’s strengths and minimize its weaknesses.

Skill Reservations with a Timeline System {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/ba0d6aa5b7e6616ef175121fddb766a1f929bc26.gif

We’ve completely removed the tedium of “auto-attacks.” In ChaosBringer, players must assign each skill manually. But it’s not inconvenient! Our innovative skill reservation system allows complex strategies with just a few clicks, inspired by the macro system in World of Warcraft.

We’ve introduced a character-specific timeline that visually displays the next actions of each character and enemy, making it easier to grasp and predict the flow of battle. It’s like being a commander in control of the entire battlefield!

We’ve also added a dynamic queue system. For example, if you move a character to avoid a boss’s strong attack, the previously reserved skills aren’t canceled. Instead, the movement command is naturally inserted into the queue. You don’t have to choose between strategy execution and immediate response.

Hex Tiles and Discrete Time {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/e211f7ffc0f4fa92f14fb328902c20a61ebbecf8.gif

Even with skill reservations, small changes in position or timing shouldn’t render strategies ineffective.

Hex Tiles To maximize the effectiveness of the skill reservation system, we’ve introduced hex tiles to spatially discretize the battlefield! This prevents skills from failing due to meaningless movement, and players don’t have to cancel reserved skills unnecessarily.

0.1-Second Time Slots For the same reason, we’ve discretized time into 0.1-second intervals. This retains the feel of real-time combat while adding strategic depth similar to turn-based games. Players can pause less often while maintaining greater control and still enjoy the tension of real-time combat.

Threat Meter System {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/6cf23227a8ff7c5fd9b7ff14ea2835680e393950.gif

As we introduced in the last dev note, we’ve implemented a core element of MMORPGs: the threat meter system. With threat and damage meters visible, tanks can hold threat, while DPS and healers can devise strategies to maximize their roles without attracting unwanted attention. Even in a single-player environment, you can enjoy the depth of party play. Remember, it’s a solo game, so there’s no pressure from raid members. Just enjoy the party play experience!

The Future of RTwP: Our Vision

One of the reasons we chose RTwP is the inspiration we drew from talented developers like Josh Sawyer, whose games have showcased RTwP’s strategic depth.

We secretly hope he plays ChaosBringer someday, and perhaps our innovative RTwP system might inspire him to create another RTwP game. If he applies his experience and creativity to RTwP again, we believe a new revolution in the genre could unfold.

With ChaosBringer, we dream of a renaissance for RTwP! We hope this game reintroduces the appeal of RTwP and brings this system’s joy to a new generation of gamers.

Our Philosophy on RTwP

Breaking the Tradeoff Between Real-Time Dynamics and Strategy

This is the core of the ChaosBringer experience. We aim to deliver both the depth of strategy and the thrill of real-time action. It’s not just a system choice; it reflects our philosophy on the experience games should offer.

In the RTwP vs. turn-based debate, we noticed that both sides value strategic depth. Turn-based fans argue that it allows for deeper strategy, while RTwP supporters highlight that strategy is still possible within the real-time tension.

Our goal is to satisfy both. Combat in ChaosBringer demands strategic thinking as profound as turn-based games, while also providing the dynamism and tension of real-time action. We’re here to prove it can be done.

In Conclusion

Look forward to ChaosBringer’s new combat system, which combines strategic depth, real-time thrill, and intuitive control! We hope this system will offer nostalgia and innovation to RTwP fans and bring turn-based combat fans a new type of strategic gameplay.

notes.title: ChaosBringer Combat System Introduction
notes.content:
Hello, I’m Chaos, the system and balance designer of ChaosBringer. In our previous article, Pencil shared the background and memories that inspired ChaosBringer’s creation.

In this article, I’ll offer a closer look at the core of ChaosBringer’s gameplay: how we brought the thrilling raid experience of MMORPGs to solo play with our unique combat system.

MMORPG-Style Raid

Our game’s raid bosses come with intricate and diverse patterns that go beyond typical designs. Each boss expects the cooperation of a tank, DPS, and healer, each fulfilling their role to the fullest. The challenge of adapting strategies to counter these patterns captures the spirit of raiding with friends. But here’s the twist—you control every character yourself!

And as any MMORPG player knows, managing even one character can be tough. So, how does it work?

RTwP System with Skill Reservations

To address this, we developed the RTwP system with skill reservations.

ChaosBringer’s combat is rooted in an RTwP (real-time with pause) system. Players can jump into real-time action but can also pause anytime to assign actions to each character. However, too much pausing can disrupt the gameplay flow, and controlling multiple characters without pauses can lead to chaotic, less strategic play.

To bridge this, ChaosBringer takes it a step further with skill reservations.

In our system, players can queue skills for each character in the timeline, creating a longer, seamless playback phase. Master each role’s skill rotation, line up the actions, and press the space bar! When you hit play, your characters deliver a coordinated, strategic performance that brings the depth of MMORPG combat to solo play. And in emergencies, you can pause anytime to adjust your plan before resuming the action.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/ba0d6aa5b7e6616ef175121fddb766a1f929bc26.gif

Damage and Threat Meters

As mentioned, our bosses call for well-coordinated strategies involving a tank, DPS, and healer. ChaosBringer incorporates a complete threat system with both damage and threat meters for players to track. Tanks can hold threat, while DPS and healers maximize their roles without drawing unwanted attention. Even in a single-player setting, you’ll feel the depth of true party dynamics. And since it’s a solo game, there’s no need to worry about low damage, low heals, or misplaced threat drawing criticism from teammates.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224210/6cf23227a8ff7c5fd9b7ff14ea2835680e393950.gif

Coming Soon

If you’d like to dive deeper into our RTwP system or learn how ChaosBringer created such a distinct combat experience, stay tuned for the next article!

notes.title: Chaos Bringer: Solo Party-Based Boss Raids
notes.content:
Introduction

Hello, I’m Pencil, the lead for boss and scenario design on ChaosBringer. Starting today, I’d like to introduce our game and share the development process through a series of posts.

First, I’m excited to share some great news! The Steam page for ChaosBringer is finally live. We’d greatly appreciate it if you could take a look, and if it piques your interest, please consider adding it to your wishlist.

Starting today, through our development diaries, we aim to share the story behind the making of our game. We’ll be bringing you more details about ChaosBringer, our ideas, challenges, and the various aspects of development. Your support and enthusiasm are a great source of motivation for us. Please join us as we watch ChaosBringer grow. We look forward to using this space to communicate more closely with you all.

Development Diary Part 1: The Origins

""Cut the DPS! Cut the DPS! Who’s still attacking?!"" If you’ve ever participated in a raid in an MMORPG, you’ve probably heard the raid leader’s urgent shout like this, or felt the frustration of having to hold back your damage, even with great gear. Remember those moments?

For those who miss the intense moments of MMORPG raids, or when your party wiped after failing a boss mechanic but everyone laughed and tried again. Or perhaps you’ve had to leave those memories behind as real life made it harder to coordinate schedules with others?

That’s where our journey began. ""What if we could experience that same thrill on our own?"" That question is what sparked the creation of ChaosBringer.

ChaosBringer is a party-based single-player RPG set in a fantasy world. In our game, you don’t control just one character. In 4-player raids, you control all 4, and in 8-player raids, you control all 8?you’re in command of the entire party.

Players can enjoy solo boss raids by gathering four or eight heroes equipped with gear of their choice, playing at their own pace. We, as fans who once enjoyed MMORPG raids, have created this game for those who want to relive that thrilling experience.

Preview In the next diary, we’ll introduce the systems we’ve implemented to make the game even more enjoyable for you.
